frontier.hypothesis: Cluster B's add is boosted only because its sole consumer is the insn just scheduled; a spelling in which the arg1+0 store is released in the same cycle (so both carry the boost and the higher-LUID-first tie-break at sched.c:2463 decides) would emit the target order.
frontier.mechanism: sched.c schedule_insn releases the dependents of the just-scheduled insn; which released insns inherit LAUNCH_PRIORITY determines the pick at the next clock.
frontier.next_probe: Read tools/gcc-2.7.2/sched.c:3650-3880 (schedule_insn) to establish exactly which released insns carry the boost, then spell only the variants that put both stores in the same release cycle and re-measure with tmp/grind/func_8006A564/s8/sweep.ps1.

frontier.hypothesis: The remaining lever is in the dependence structure AROUND cluster B's group rather than in its text (28 local spellings measured dead), e.g. whether tile (the obj2->0x1C record pointer) is held live across the first func_8007352C call or re-derived after it.
frontier.mechanism: Re-deriving the record pointer after the call changes which insns are ready in the same cycle as the two stores, which is the only input to the scheduler's pick that the C can still move.
frontier.next_probe: Spell 4-6 variants that re-derive `tile = *(u8 **)(obj2 + 0x1C);` (or re-read it from arg0) between the two func_8007352C calls, measure each, and verify with tmp/grind/func_8006A564/s8/objdiff.sh that cluster A stays closed.

frontier.hypothesis: Cluster A's closure is fragile to edits elsewhere in the body; any future change must be validated instruction-for-instruction, not by score alone.
frontier.mechanism: Blocks 1-3 and cluster A now match exactly, so a spelling change anywhere in the final block can silently trade cluster A's 4 insns for cluster B's 3 and leave the score looking flat.
frontier.next_probe: Run tmp/grind/func_8006A564/s8/objdiff.sh (it needs a prior `sandbox --disable all` run) after every edit and confirm the only `!!` rows are the 3 cluster-B lines plus the 8 branch/jump displacement rows.
